what_it_does.name: security-review
what_it_does.summary: Instructions and reference guides for a security code review of a file, diff or component the user names. The agent researches the whole codebase to trace data flow, upstream validation and framework protections, then reports only high-confidence exploitable vulnerabilities with location, impact, evidence and fix, and notes medium-confidence ones as needing verification. Seventeen OWASP-derived vulnerability references, Python and JavaScript framework guides and a Dockerfile guide are loaded by code type. Use it when asked for a security review, to find vulnerabilities or for an OWASP review.
tasks: review a file, diff or component for exploitable vulnerabilities
trace data flow to confirm attacker-controlled input before flagging
classify findings by severity and confidence
check Django, Flask, FastAPI, Express, React, Vue and Next.js patterns
report findings in a fixed format with a fix for each

outputs.what: security review report with summary, findings and items that need verification
outputs.form: Markdown text in the fixed Security Review format, with VULN and VERIFY entries

outputs.what: a fix for each high-confidence finding
outputs.form: a Fix line in each finding

outputs.what: a statement that nothing was found

inputs.type: a file, diff, pull request or component the user names

inputs.what: the surrounding codebase, with settings, config files and middleware

when_input_is_missing.case: the code is in a language other than Python or JavaScript
when_input_is_missing.behaviour: no dedicated guide is loaded, the references/ files are used and framework protections are verified in the codebase

when_input_is_missing.case: the django-access-review skill is not available for Django access control
the gha-security-review skill is not available for GitHub Actions workflows

exclusions: not for GitHub Actions workflow exploitation, which belongs to the gha-security-review skill
not for in-depth Django access-control review of permission classes and endpoint scopes
not for Kubernetes, Terraform or cloud IAM configuration review
not for running scanners, fuzzers or dynamic testing tools
not for general code review or performance review
not for writing exploits against systems the user does not own

vulnerabilities.finding: Malware, install-time execution, base64 payloads, secret harvesting, exfiltration and a reverse shell to attacker.com:4444
vulnerabilities.fix: treat the package as compromised and avoid installation, rotate exposed secrets and revoke tokens possibly present in CI/CD environments

risks.risk: Installing the skill brings in references/supply-chain.md, which C3 rates as malware for its install-hook, exfiltration and reverse shell code, while C2 reads the same code as red flags for the auditor.
risks.severity: HIGH by C3, SAFE overall by C2
risks.mitigation: none stated, C2 notes the code sits under Malicious Package Indicators as detection examples

risks.risk: Secrets, customer data or PII found in the reviewed code can end up in the report or be stored, since each finding quotes the vulnerable code as evidence.
risks.mitigation: a rule that secrets, customer data and PII are not stored, an instruction only

risks.risk: Instructions planted in comments or files of the reviewed codebase reach an agent that holds Bash, since the whole codebase is read without boundary markers.

limitations: Language coverage beyond Python and JavaScript relies on language-agnostic references, so framework-specific mitigations in Go, Rust, Java, PHP and Ruby may be missed or over-flagged.
Infrastructure coverage is limited to Dockerfiles, and Kubernetes, Terraform and cloud IAM review produce generic results.
On very large codebases the research step can be incomplete and findings may land in Needs Verification more often.
The reference material is a derivative of the OWASP cheat sheets at a point in time and does not track upstream revisions automatically.
